slides.label: THE IDEA
slides.headline: A fax machine {saleswoman} had a problem.
slides.body: Sara Blakely had *never taken a business class* or worked in fashion. She wanted to avoid panty lines without a bulky girdle, so she *cut the feet off* control-top pantyhose.

slides.label: THE PITCH
rows: Her *savings*, she has said, from selling fax machines. That was the budget.
She got *ten minutes* with Neiman Marcus buyers, and paid her own flight to Dallas.
She mailed Oprah a *prototype and a handwritten note.* Oprah later named Spanx a favorite product.

slides.label: THE RULE
slides.headline: She never took a {single investor.}
slides.body: Blakely launched with *no outside investors* and, Stanford GSB reports, kept *100% ownership.* In *2012,* Forbes named her the *youngest self-made female billionaire.*

slides.label: THE EXIT
slides.headline: Then Blackstone {bought in.}
slides.body: In *2021,* Blackstone bought a *majority stake* at a *$1.2 billion* valuation. Blakely kept a significant stake and stayed on as executive chairwoman. ==Not bad for $5,000.==

last.headline: Solve {your own annoying problem,} and keep control.
last.body: Blakely's first big asset wasn't money. It was a problem she knew better than anyone. Which would you rather have: a big check or full control?
